'''Yabula-Yabula''' (Jabulajabula) in an extinct language of [[Australia]], located in [[Victoria (state)|Victoria]] and [[New South Wales]]. Dixon listed it an [[language isolate|isolate]], but ''Glottolog'' evaluates it as a dialect of [[Yorta Yorta language|Yotayota]].<ref>Heather Bowe and Stephen Morey. 1999. The Yorta Yorta (Bangerang) Language of the Murray Goulborn including Yabula Yabula. (Pacific Linguistics: Series C, 154.) Canberra: Research School of Pacific and Asian Studies, Australian National University.</ref> It shares only 44% of its vocabulary with Yorta Yorta, so is best considered a separate language. This may be due to the rapid lexical change involved after a person's death, as their name then cannot be uttered.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Bowe |first=Heather J. |url=https://openresearch-repository.anu.edu.au/bitstream/1885/146615/1/PL-C154.pdf |title=The Yorta Yorta (Bangerang) language of the Murray Goulburn: including Yabula Yabula |last2=Morey |first2=Stephen |date=1999 |publisher=Pacific Linguistics, Research School of Pacific and Asian Studies, the Australian National University |isbn=978-0-85883-513-9 |series=Pacific linguistics, Series C |location=Canberra |language=en-AU |oclc=ocm40792250}}</ref>
